idea: Builders stripped the soil and quarried the fissured knoll under the site; extraction scars match the wall stones (on-site quarry).
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Duos Nuraghes vol.1 (BAR IS 949); Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia
scenario_label: S5a_onsite; S1b_joints_low/high; REALISTIC and MOST_REALISTIC (joints_low on outcrop); hybrid stone rule (4,940 sites on own outcrop)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Quarry faces or extraction steps within 200 m of the tower, same lithology as the walls, at roughly the share of sites the model puts on their own outcrop (68.9%).

idea: Extraction along natural joints with stone mauls, wetted wooden wedges and wooden levers.
author: Webster; Serra
work: Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia [IT-wt]; Cave megalitiche della Sardegna, ArcheoArte 4
evidence_type: Webster: inference from Duos evidence; Serra: survey of (Neolithic) menhir quarries, one nuraghe link
FIELD_PREDICTION: Wedge sockets, stepped extraction faces and lever scars on outcrops next to nuraghi; an experimental wedge-and-lever extraction of local basalt should take about 11-17.5 person-hours per m3.

idea: Stone and wooden tools only; bronze tools probably not in common use in the Early and Middle Bronze Age.
author: Webster (citing Lo Schiavo 1986)
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
numbers_with_locator: Erasmus 1965 quarry rate 2,700 kg/man-day with hardwood bar; 8,000 with iron bar (Webster 1991: 852)
scenario_label: All scenarios (every quarry rate is a non-metal rate); C2_day5 / v11 5-h day for the Erasmus rate
FIELD_PREDICTION: No metal tool marks on Middle Bronze Age tower blocks; percussion and wedge marks only.

idea: Much stone was collected from the surface (free-stones, scree, field clearance) rather than quarried.
author: Webster; Araque Gonzalez; Lilliu & Zucca
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Monuments of cooperating communities (ISLANDIA, Artemide); Su Nuraxi di Barumini
evidence_type: Webster: field observation (Borore); Araque: OPINION; Lilliu & Zucca: excavation reading (Su Nuraxi phase a stones from the slope)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Blocks with weathered cortex and no fresh fracture faces; no quarry faces near sites built off outcrop.

idea: Building nuraghi cleared rocky land for farming; nuraghe density tracks stoniness, and many complex nuraghi side by side may mark very stony ground.
author: Araque Gonzalez
work: Monuments of cooperating communities: Sardinian nuraghi and sanctuaries (ISLANDIA)
implementation: (a) Post hoc: regress nuraghe density (5 km cells) on a stoniness proxy (outcrop share and stony lithologies from the ARPAS map) and on the model scree share. (b) Mechanism: scree available per catchment = catchment ha (tools/food_capacity.py Thiessen catchments) x surface-stone yield Y; a site collects scree until the budget is spent, then quarries.
ranges_and_sources: Y = 10 / 50 / 200 t per ha: ASSUMPTION (no published yield); catchment radius 1.5 km (S12 central)
realism_reason: Clearance as a stone source is plausible (Q04), but there is no surface-stone yield figure and the density link is untested.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Nuraghe and complex-nuraghe density rise with surface stoniness after controlling for soil quality; land around nuraghi is cleared of loose stone compared with similar empty terrain.

idea: An ancient limestone quarry lies a short distance from a nuraghe (Ussassai, on the tacco).
author: Anonymous (municipal census report)
work: Relazione riassuntiva sul censimento di monumenti archeologici (Ussassai)
page: page not recoverable (Catalogue chunk, item no. 49)
FIELD_PREDICTION: The quarry is Bronze Age and its block sizes match the nuraghe; a date (stratified tools or sediments) would confirm it.

idea: Su Nuraxi quadrilobe and first antemural used >4,000 m3 of basalt, partly collected on the Giara slope and partly quarried on the plateau edge; the later raising added ~13,000 m3.
author: Tagliagambe (reporting an unnamed 1995 survey)
work: L'identita del popolo sardo e i "beni nuragici": dieci presupposti (nurnet.net)
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY: Tagliagambe 2024 reports a 1995 estimate whose author is not named
scenario_label: S7_webster_classes (6,700 t = 2,800 m3 bastioned); S13_high; S10
FIELD_PREDICTION: A photogrammetric volume survey of Su Nuraxi should give the phase volumes; mixed collected and quarried blocks in the quadrilobe.

idea: Most blocks were set with little or no dressing in rough polygonal (cyclopean) courses.
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
scenario_label: S2a_unworked; REALISTIC / MOST_REALISTIC (no dressing for single towers)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Tool-dressed faces absent or rare on single towers; dressing waste scarce in their construction layers.

idea: Dressing went mainly into the smaller stones of the upper inner vault courses, where ring friction between fitted blocks gives the tholos its strength.
author: Webster; Laner
work: Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia [IT-wt]; Accabadora. Tecnologia delle costruzioni nuragiche
evidence_type: OPINION grounded in masonry observation and statics
implementation: Dress only the inner tholos vault courses of every tower: dressed volume = share v of the tower blocks (inner ring above the springing) at Boswinkel dressing rates; replaces "no dressing" for single towers and adds to Webster/fine facing elsewhere.
ranges_and_sources: v = 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.30 of blocks (ASSUMPTION from geometry: vault 6-8 m of a 15 m tower, Webster 2015: 51; inner ring only); dressing 57-62 ph/m3 (Boswinkel 2021: 120-121, Table 7.8)
realism_reason: Matches the observed concentration of worked blocks in vaults; only the share is assumed.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Worked (trapezoidal, hammer-dressed) faces cluster in the inner vault courses; dressing chips concentrate in the tower fill at vault levels.

idea: Fine squared courses in the upper keep and sub-squared bastion blocks with rubble-packed joints at Santu Antine; large chisel-finished blocks only high up.
author: Contu
work: Il Nuraghe Santu Antine
scenario_label: S2b_fine; REALISTIC / MOST_REALISTIC (fine facing >= 3 towers); C3_dress
FIELD_PREDICTION: Fine dressing restricted to complexes and upper courses; block size data from Santu Antine reproduce the model block distribution for complexes.

idea: Isodomic and bichrome masonry was intended from the design stage, especially for the summit parts; present from the first building phases.
author: Paglietti & Mulas
work: Statica ed estetica. Architetture isodome e bicrome in eta nuragica (Layers 8)
evidence_type: Survey and re-reading of excavation reports (Su Nuraxi tower C, Santu Antine, Puttu de Inza)
scenario_label: S2b_fine / HIGH (upper bound: fine facing on complexes); the stone-sourcing side is G05 (S23_bichrome)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Squared, hammer-dressed blocks of a contrasting stone in the collapse at the foot of towers, from the first building phase.

idea: Rough-shaping was done on site: angular basalt chips and a hammerstone lie in the lowest strata of both Duos towers.
author: Webster
work: Duos Nuraghes vol. 1 [IT-wt]
scenario_label: All scenarios haul undressed block mass (site dressing). The quarry-dressing alternative (less mass hauled) is not run and is contradicted by this evidence.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Dressing debris in foundation and early construction layers inside and around towers, not only at quarries.

idea: About 3,000 blocks per single tower; median 75x50x50 cm (0.19 m3, ~450 kg); range <0.06 to ~1 m3 (~2.4 t).
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
numbers_with_locator: 3,000 blocks; 0.19 m3; 450 kg; 1,350 t per tower (852, Table 1)
scenario_label: baseline block draw; TOST block_median_kg and block_sigma ends
FIELD_PREDICTION: Photogrammetric block counts on standing single towers give ~3,000 blocks with a median near 0.19 m3.

idea: Block size decreases with height: big polyhedral boulders in the base, smaller stones in middle and upper courses; above 3-4 m stones could be carried by hand.
author: Webster; Laner; Scintu; Mossa et al.
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Accabadora; Le torri del cielo; Interventi presso il nuraghe S'Ulimu (Quaderni 35)
page: Webster 1991: 851; Laner 1999: 30; Scintu 2003: 247; Mossa et al. 2024: page not recoverable
evidence_type: EVIDENCE: masonry survey at many towers
implementation: (1) Make the lever and stair lift cost mass-proportional: 0.37 ph x (piece mass / 450 kg) per course climbed (ASSUMPTION). (2) Assign pieces to courses in descending mass order (graded) instead of the current random order. Run (1) alone and (1)+(2) to separate rate and ordering effects.
ranges_and_sources: lever 0.37 ph per block per 0.9 m course (Boswinkel 2021: 124); mass scaling ASSUMPTION; course count 17 (model geometry, FREE)
extends: MOST_REALISTIC_P10 (S4 lift; also covers F02 foundation boulders)
realism_reason: Grading is observed at most surveyed towers; the mass-proportional lift rate is an assumption.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Course-by-course block volume falls with height in photogrammetric surveys; in an experiment, lever-lift time per course rises with block mass.

idea: Very heavy single pieces (entrance lintels, base blocks) of 1.5-3+ t could not be split and had to be moved whole.
author: Webster; Murru; Lilliu
work: Duos Nuraghes vol. 1; L'architettura e la stratigrafia muraria di Nuraxi 'e Cresia (in Perra & Cicilloni eds); Il nuraghe di Barumini e la stratigrafia nuragica
implementation: Add per tower one unsplittable lintel piece (and optionally two relief-window lintels of 0.5 t). Its haul crew = ceil(mass / pull per person) must be assembled at once; small parties must obtain join help or wait (log seasons waited). Fallback after N seasons: lever-walking at the M4 rate.
ranges_and_sources: lintel 1.5 / 3.0 / 4.2 t (Webster 2001: 21; Murru 2018: 229); pull 100 kg (mu 0.3) or 78.9 kg (mu 0.38) per person (model); N = 5 seasons (FREE)
realism_reason: Every tower has a lintel; masses are measured. The waiting rule is assumed.
FIELD_PREDICTION: TWR1 communities of 3-20 workers cannot haul a 3-t lintel alone (30-40 haulers needed): expect lintels quarried closest to the site or help from neighbours. In an experiment, count the crew needed to move a 3-t lintel.

idea: Blocks moved on sledges over rollers, man- or ox-hauled with tow ropes (method Lilliu used in restoring Su Nuraxi).
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia
reported_only: Lilliu & Zucca 1988 restoration practice reported by Webster 1991: 849
scenario_label: S3a_rails_tallow; S3b_rails_grease; S3c_dry_ground; C1_rails; C1_rails_relay (relay crew as roller/slipway handlers)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Drag tracks or prepared slipways between quarry and site; in an experiment, a roller sledge crew per tonne close to 10 people.

idea: Rollers and pulleys rejected: blocks were levered, dragged on sledges or carried on stretchers.
author: Laner
work: Accabadora
FIELD_PREDICTION: No roller or pulley wear traces; sledge-drag or lever marks only.

idea: Cattle traction may not have been common before the Late Bronze Age, so early towers were man-hauled.
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
FIELD_PREDICTION: Pathological draught lesions on cattle bones appear only in LBA contexts.

idea: Sled hauling needs about 2 men per tonne on level ground (Atkinson); 9 men per tonne up a 9 degree incline on sled-over-rollers.
author: Webster (citing Atkinson 1961)
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
scenario_label: S3b_rails_grease (mu 0.05 ~ 2 men/t); slope penalty of the drag raster
FIELD_PREDICTION: An experimental sled-over-rollers haul of 1 t on level ground needs ~2 haulers.

idea: Man-hauling with tumpline and sled over <=200 m at 1,200 kg per man-day (Erasmus).
author: Webster (citing Erasmus 1965: 286-7)
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
FIELD_PREDICTION: Short-haul experiment reproduces ~1.2 t per 5-h person-day.

idea: Wheeled carts with solid wheels (two-ox carts) moved stone.
author: Ugas; Tagliagambe
work: Shardana e Sardegna; nurnet.net article
page: Ugas 2016: page not recoverable; Tagliagambe: web, no page
implementation: LBA complexes (TWR >= 3) haul routes > 1 km by ox wagon at Boswinkel costings; oxen-hours reported separately.
ranges_and_sources: 1.67 km/h loaded, 2.5 km/h empty, 12 oxen per 5 t (Boswinkel 2021: 114-118, App. 4 p. 210)
realism_reason: No direct evidence of carts in nuraghe building; cattle traction itself is late (T03).
FIELD_PREDICTION: Bronze Age cart ruts dated between quarries and complex nuraghi; wheel or cart parts in LBA contexts.

idea: Coastal stone and people moved by sea.
author: (authors' request; analogue Hazell & Fitzpatrick 2006)
work: Archaeology in Oceania 41: 12-24
FIELD_PREDICTION: Coastal nuraghi with stone from coastal outcrops across a bay rather than nearer inland outcrops; landing places with block debris.

idea: River transport of building stone (rafting).
author: Montalbano (blog)
work: Navigazione antica fluviale e marittima (pierluigimontalbano.blogspot.com)
not_testable_reason: Data missing: no evidence of Bronze Age navigability of Sardinian rivers or of river-borne building stone.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Nuraghi along the Tirso or Flumendosa with stone from upstream outcrops not reachable more cheaply overland.

idea: Prepared or shared trackways (rail-like tracks, slipways) built along long routes.
author: (model families; GEN 65)
work: literature/general_energetics_logistics.md line 65
scenario_label: A4_trust_track; A5_full; P_G20_kmesh4_track; MOST_REALISTIC (rails > 1 km); C1_rails
FIELD_PREDICTION: Linear trackway features (stone-free strips, timber sockets) between distant quarries and complexes such as S'Urachi.

idea: Some large complexes in stone-poor zones used stone brought from km away (S'Urachi basalt from outcrops ~3 km away; complexes planned "almost as small capitals").
author: Stiglitz, Puliga, Usai, Carboni & Lecca; Lo Schiavo, Perra, Usai et al.
work: Atti XLIV RS IIPP III; Scienze dell'Antichita 15
page: Stiglitz et al. 2012: 921-922; Lo Schiavo et al. 2009: page via NUR review (n. 25)
scenario_label: S5c_complex_far (>= 3 km for TWR >= 3); hybrid stone rule (recorded stone)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Petrographic provenance of S'Urachi and other stone-poor complexes to outcrops ~3 km away; model haul for these sites should match.

idea: Nuraghi of San Gavino Monreale (Campidano) lie up to 10 km from their stone source.
author: Unattributed quotation (blog; wording suggests Ugas)
work: "Hierarchies nuragiques", Sardegna verso l'Unesco blog
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY: unattributed quotation in a blog
implementation: Post hoc: read the hybrid-rule haul of the San Gavino Monreale sites from the MR_P10 summary and compare with 10 km.
realism_reason: Unverified source; a useful outlier check of the stone rule.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Petrographic provenance of San Gavino nuraghe blocks to sources 5-10 km away.

idea: External earthen ramp or inclined plane against the outer wall, perhaps from soil cleared from the site and planked.
author: Lilliu; Webster
work: I nuraghi (via Laner 1999: 28-29); Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia
numbers_with_locator: ramp to first storey ~45 m long at 1:6.5 (Webster 1991: 851)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Compacted ramp fill or ramp retaining walls against tower bases in excavated sections.

idea: A ramp at the stair slope would need about as much material as the tower; it could serve only the first 3-4 m, above which stones (smaller there) were carried on stretchers.
author: Laner
work: Accabadora
implementation: Earth ramp to h0 (straight, S4b arithmetic: V = w h0^2 / (2 s)), then pieces above h0 lifted at the internal-stair/stretcher rate (S4c rate) per piece.
ranges_and_sources: h0 = 3 / 4 m (Laner 1999: 30); ramp width 3 m, slope 20%, earth 13.02 ph/m3 incl. build and removal (S4b, GEN 68, 78, 205): 67.5 m3 (879 ph) at 3 m, 120 m3 (1,562 ph) at 4 m
realism_reason: Mechanically sound and fits the size grading (D07); no excavated ramp yet.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Ramp deposits only in the lowest 3-4 m around tower bases; an experiment can time stretcher carrying of <= 300 kg blocks by six people up a 25-30% stair.

idea: Spiral ramp built against the tower as it rose, reinforced with timber beams set in putlog holes; a rising line of putlog holes at 12% survives on tower 3 of S'Urachi.
author: Stiglitz, Dies Cusi et al.
work: Intorno al nuraghe: notizie preliminari sul progetto S'Urachi (Quaderni 26/2015)
evidence_type: EVIDENCE: survey of putlog holes (20x10 cm) + interpretation
numbers_with_locator: slope 12%; height ~7.5 m; width >3 m at base to ~1.5 m at top; holes ~20x10 cm (198-199)
implementation: Ramp leaning on the tower: length L = h / 0.12, width tapering 3 -> 1.5 m, volume = 0.12 L^2 (469 m3 to 7.5 m; 1,875 m3 to 15 m), costed at the S4b earth rate (13.02 ph/m3, build + removal; timber unpriced). Variant _7m5: ramp to 7.5 m, internal stair above; _full: ramp to the full 15 m.
ranges_and_sources: slope 12%, height 7.5 m, widths 3 / 1.5 m (Stiglitz et al. 2015: 198-199); earth rates GEN 68, 78, 205
realism_reason: Physical traces at one site, interpreted by the excavators; untested elsewhere.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Rising lines of ~20x10 cm putlog holes at ~12% gradient on outer tower faces, and stepped buttress bonding on one side, at other towers.

idea: External wooden spiral ramp ("scalandrone di legno") fixed into oblique hollows in the wall (Corbos-Silanus, Succoronis-Macomer).
author: Manca 1983; Sanna 1986; Lilliu 1966 (all via Laner)
work: Accabadora
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY: Manca, Sanna and Lilliu 1966 reported by Laner 1999: 28-29
numbers_with_locator: Laner: 2 m ramp, 300 kg block + 6 men, ~3,000 kgm, beams ~35 cm (32-33)
not_testable_reason: Data missing: no timber felling/working rate in the sources, and Laner shows the structure impractical.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Regular oblique sockets of beam size on several towers, rising in a helix.

idea: Counterweight lifting.
author: Oppes 1988 (via Laner)
work: Accabadora
not_testable_reason: No mechanism or rate specified in an accessible source.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Anchor sockets or pivot settings at tower tops.

idea: Timber frame with winch or pulley, powered by yoked oxen.
author: Scintu; Moreu 1990 (via Laner)
work: Le torri del cielo; Accabadora
not_testable_reason: Data missing: no Bronze Age pulley or tackle, no lift rate; cattle traction late (T03).
FIELD_PREDICTION: Pulley sheaves, rope wear grooves on corbels, or post settings for a frame around towers.

idea: The intramural stair was the builders' ramp: the nuraghe as "machine of itself", no scaffolding.
author: Laner
work: Accabadora
evidence_type: OPINION (engineering argument); problem cases: stairs starting 4-5 m up, Duos A without stair (44)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Wear on stair treads and wall faces at load-carrying height; stair geometry continuous from the ground in most towers.

idea: Counter-opinion: an internal ramp is geometrically impossible; an external ramp is too costly; operational chains should be tested in the field.
author: Satta 2010 (quoted by Atzeni & Frau)
work: Atzeni & Frau 2023 (book chapter compilation)
scenario_label: S4b_ramp vs S4c_internal_stair (comparison already in the paper)
FIELD_PREDICTION: As L01 and L07.

idea: Course-by-course levering of blocks; the tower rose level by level.
author: Webster; Cavanagh & Laxton 1987 (via Webster); Bortolussi et al.
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; A study on the stability and construction techniques of nuragic towers (Int. J. Archit. Herit.)
numbers_with_locator: lever 0.37 ph per block per course (Boswinkel 2021: 124)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Irregular, spiralling and abruptly ending courses (as Gallin observed); lever notches on block edges.

idea: Scaffolding by carpenters, and cranes or block-and-tackle, were among the needed roles.
author: Araque Gonzalez
work: Monuments of cooperating communities
not_testable_reason: Data missing: no timber rate or scaffold design; contradicted by Laner 1999: 33 (no scaffolding).
FIELD_PREDICTION: Putlog holes in regular grids (not in a rising helix, cf. L03).

idea: The tholos was corbelled without centring; no keystone; the dome can be left open at any ring.
author: Laner
work: Accabadora
scenario_label: Implicit in all scenarios (no centring cost). The centring alternative is NOT TESTABLE (no rate).
FIELD_PREDICTION: No post settings on chamber floors under vaults.

idea: Inner shell first, outer ring later (vs simultaneous rise of both faces).
author: Santillo Frizell 1987 (via Bortolussi et al.)
work: Bortolussi et al. 2025
reported_only: Santillo Frizell 1987 via Bortolussi et al. 2025: 12
not_testable_reason: No labour or spatial consequence at the model grain (same stone, same lift).
FIELD_PREDICTION: Straight vertical joints between inner and outer faces in collapsed sections.

idea: Placing rates of 7-15 blocks per hour with 7 lifters per 300 kg block; tower in 250 days with 16 haulers, 40 + 20 builders and 1 master.
author: Montalbano (blog)
work: Costruiamo un nuraghe da noi in otto mesi; In quanto tempo e possibile costruire un nuraghe?
scenario_label: Placing rate 0.47-1.0 ph per block lies inside C3_set_low / C3_set_high (4.95-10 ph/m3 x 0.19 m3 = 0.94-1.9 ph per block)
FIELD_PREDICTION: An experimental build (NurTime) will measure placing rates per block.

idea: Soil was stripped (1-2 m) to bedrock before building; the cleared dirt could feed an earthen ramp.
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Duos Nuraghes vol. 1
implementation: Site preparation task before tower 1: strip footprint x depth at the earth rate (dig + carry, no removal). Variant _ramp: the stripped volume is credited against the S4b ramp earth (digging not paid twice).
ranges_and_sources: footprint 113 m2 per tower (model cone, 12 m base: FREE); depth 1 / 2 m (Webster 1991: 848); dig 4.2 ph/m3 + carry 0.71 ph/m3 (GEN 68, 78, 205) = 555-1,110 ph per tower
realism_reason: Directly attested at Duos; footprint and depth range are simple.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Cuts through soil to bedrock under tower foundations; spoil reused in ramps or platform fill.

idea: A foundation platform of large boulders, gaps filled with graded rubble (finer upwards); a protruding foundation course at S'Urachi towers 2-3.
author: Webster; Stiglitz, Dies Cusi et al.
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Duos Nuraghes vol. 1; Quaderni 26/2015
page: Webster 1991: 849; Webster 2001: 123; Stiglitz et al. 2015: page not recoverable (same article, before p. 198)
implementation: Covered by the graded assignment of D07: the heaviest pieces form the ground course (no lift).
ranges_and_sources: as D07
realism_reason: Excavated at Duos and S'Urachi.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Largest blocks of each tower in the ground course; graded rubble in foundation gaps.

idea: Nuraghi generally have no foundations; their mass makes them superfluous.
author: Idini 2015 (quoted by Atzeni & Frau)
work: Atzeni & Frau 2023
scenario_label: All current scenarios (no foundation cost); contrast with S15_found
FIELD_PREDICTION: Towers set directly on soil without cut or platform.

idea: Small wedge stones (zeppe) level the beds; packing is part of setting.
author: Webster; Laner
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Accabadora
evidence_type: EVIDENCE: masonry survey; rate from experiment (Abrams)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Wedge stones in every bed joint; experiment confirms packing time is within the walling rate.

idea: Stones were bedded in a clay or mud mortar with careful chinking (dry masonry only in name).
author: Vanzetti, Castangia, Depalmas, Ialongo, Leonelli, Perra, Usai; Mossa et al.; Stiglitz, Dies Cusi et al.; Araque Gonzalez
work: Complessi fortificati della Sardegna (Sc. Antichita 19); S'Ulimu (Quaderni 35); S'Urachi (Quaderni 26); ISLANDIA
page: Vanzetti et al. 2013: 89; Mossa et al. 2024: page not recoverable; Stiglitz et al. 2015: 198; Araque Gonzalez 2021: 193
evidence_type: EVIDENCE: survey of masonry at several sites
implementation: Add a mortar task per tower: mortar volume = share m of wall volume (566 m3 per tower x density factor), labour = dig + mix/water + carry, plus lift with the blocks (no extra pieces).
ranges_and_sources: m = 0.05 / 0.15 (ASSUMPTION: no measured share); dig 4.2 ph/m3 (GEN 68); mixing and water 2 ph/m3 (ASSUMPTION); carry 0.71 ph/m3 (GEN 78) -> ~195-586 ph per tower
realism_reason: Mud bedding is attested at several sites; the volume share and mixing rate are assumed.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Clay or mud residues in bed joints (micromorphology), sourced from local clay within a few hundred metres; an experiment measures mortar preparation hours per m3.

idea: Loose granular fill (sacco murario) between the tholos and the outer wall, placed and compacted in horizontal layers as both faces rose; it carries part of the load.
author: Bortolussi, Dentoni, Levanti, Cara, Pinna & Grosso; Puddu
work: A study on the stability and construction techniques of nuragic towers; Il nuraghe Littoleri a Gavoi
page: Bortolussi et al. 2025: 12-13; Puddu 2014: page not recoverable
evidence_type: EVIDENCE: mechanical (DEM) modelling + excavated wall sections
implementation: A share f of each tower's mass is rubble fill: sourced from quarry and dressing waste at the face (rubble rate 2.0 ph/m3), carried in ~20 kg loads (no sledge crews), set at the rubble assembly rate, lifted by carrying on the stair; only the facing blocks go through sledge transport and lever lift.
ranges_and_sources: f = 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.5 (ASSUMPTION); rubble 2.0 ph/m3 (Boswinkel 2021: 108); set 6.29 ph/m3 (Boswinkel 2021: 125, Table 7.11); carrying ~20 kg loads (Erasmus 1965: 287 via Turner 2018: 200)
realism_reason: Two-face walls with a fill core are the norm; only the share is assumed.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Collapsed sections show two faces with a rubble/earth core in compacted layers; core lithology = waste of the facing stone.

idea: The upper parts were finished with smaller stones and compressed clay bricks (S'Urachi).
author: Chiri & Novelli
work: Studies and projects for the archaeological park of the nuraghe S'Urachi
page: page not recoverable (near p. 828 in the Catalogue text)
evidence_type: OPINION (architects' reading; source of the claim not given in the chunk)
implementation: Replace the top h_b of each tower body by mudbrick made on site (no stone haul or lever lift for that share; earth dig + moulding labour; bricks carried up the stair).
ranges_and_sources: h_b = 2 / 4 m (ASSUMPTION); mudbrick 1,600 kg/m3 (ASSUMPTION, as S4b earth); moulding 4 ph/m3 (ASSUMPTION; no source)
realism_reason: Contested: at Pidighi brick fragments are far too few to be structural (Usai 2013, Quaderni, page not recoverable).
FIELD_PREDICTION: Brick fragments or dissolved clay in tower collapse layers in volumes proportional to the missing upper body.

idea: The keep was always built first; additions (bastion, towers) abut it without bonding; many complexes began as single towers.
author: Contu; Lilliu; Lilliu & Zucca; Melis; Puddu, Rodriguez Azogue et al.
work: Il Nuraghe Santu Antine; Il nuraghe di Barumini; Su Nuraxi di Barumini; La Sardegna nuragica (Corpora); Proyecto Nuraghe (Quaderni 26)
evidence_type: EVIDENCE: excavation and masonry stratigraphy (Santu Antine, Su Nuraxi, Candelargiu)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Straight joints between keep and additions; radiocarbon dates of addition foundations later than keep foundations.

idea: Many complexes were a single unified project (keep + added bodies), though built keep-first; a 5-tower bastion (Arrubiu) dates to one construction phase.
author: Melis; Vanzetti et al.; anonymous Arrubiu guide
work: La Sardegna nuragica (Corpora); Sc. Antichita 19; Guida al nuraghe Arrubiu
page: Melis 2017: 40-42; Vanzetti et al. 2013: ~89; Arrubiu guide: no page
evidence_type: EVIDENCE: masonry stratigraphy; Arrubiu date from excavation (guide)
reported_only: Arrubiu phase date (mid-14th c. BC) from an anonymous visitor guide
FIELD_PREDICTION: Bonded courses between keep and bastion; single-phase dates for keep and bastion.

idea: Single towers were designed so they could later be turned into multi-tower bastions (and their occupants into canton chiefs).
author: Ugas (summarised in Moravetti, Melis, Foddai & Alba)
work: La Sardegna preistorica / Le fonti scritte (compilation)
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY: Ugas's model as summarised in Moravetti et al. 2009 (primary Ugas 2005 not read)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Prepared springing points or blocked doorways on single towers for later additions.

idea: Protonuraghi (corridor nuraghi) came first, before tholos towers (overlap debated).
author: Ugas; Melis; Webster; Moravetti
work: Shardana e Sardegna; Civilta nuragica; Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia; La Sardegna nuragica
FIELD_PREDICTION: Radiocarbon dates of corridor nuraghi earlier than tholos towers in the same area.

idea: A corridor nuraghe was grafted onto an earlier Monte Claro wall and built over a hut (Sa Mandra Manna, Tula).
author: Basoli & Doro 2012 (via Usai et al.)
work: Quaderni 33/2022
page: Usai et al. 2022: page not recoverable; Basoli & Doro 2012: 601-606
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY: Basoli & Doro 2012 via Usai et al. 2022
not_testable_reason: Data missing: no count of nuraghi built on earlier walls; the stone saving cannot be assigned to sites.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Pre-Nuragic walls under nuraghe foundations at more sites.

idea: Re-facing (rifascio): a casing wall ~3 m thick and ~7 m high wrapped the Su Nuraxi bastion in the 12th-10th c. BC; a rifascio wraps the Arrubiu keep.
author: Melis; Lo Schiavo & Sanges; Lilliu
work: La Sardegna nuragica (Corpora); Il nuraghe Arrubiu di Orroli; Il nuraghe di Barumini
page: Melis 2017: ~42; Lo Schiavo & Sanges 1994: page not recoverable; Lilliu 1955: 158
numbers_with_locator: 3 m x 7 m (Melis 2017: ~42); casing blocks avg 0.12 m3 / 360 kg, some ~3 t (Lilliu 1955: 158)
implementation: Extra masonry unit (S13 extra_units) after the bastion on complexes: volume = bastion perimeter x 7 m x 3 m x fill 0.8.
ranges_and_sources: perimeter 80 / 120 m (ASSUMPTION, between Palmavera and Su Nuraxi plans); 7 m x 3 m (Melis 2017: ~42); share of complexes >= 4 towers re-faced 0.2 / 0.5 (ASSUMPTION)
realism_reason: Attested at the two best-excavated complexes; frequency unknown.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Casing walls with straight joints against earlier faces and blocked entrances, dated later than the bastion.

idea: Household or kin-group self-build over years; one tower per homestead built as the population grew by fission.
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia
scenario_label: A0_alone; MOST_REALISTIC_alone_*; MR work party (TWR1 3-20 workers)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Domestic refuse from the first occupation in single towers; build spans of a few years.

idea: Egalitarian cantonal communities of extended families, 10-20 people per nuraghe.
author: Trump (summarised by Perra)
work: La Sardegna nuragica. Storia e materiali (Moravetti, Alba, Foddai eds)
scenario_label: MR work party TWR1 5-40 residents; P_G3_canton_*
FIELD_PREDICTION: Small single-tower villages of a few houses.

idea: Heterarchical cooperation: village plus neighbours by mutual aid, no corvee; site management shifts by stage; complexes need several communities.
author: Araque Gonzalez; Schirru & Vanzetti; Rothenberg et al.
work: ISLANDIA; PLOS ONE 18: e0289023; J. Field Archaeology 49
page: Araque Gonzalez 2021: 193-195; Schirru & Vanzetti 2023: article (no page); Rothenberg et al. 2024: 356-370
evidence_type: OPINION supported by settlement survey (Schirru, Rothenberg)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Help flows of a few km and hubs at large complexes (model); no elite storage or prestige goods concentrated at builders' hubs.

idea: Two-tier: simple nuraghi built by local village masons; regular complexes need mature planning and a large, skilled, mobilised workforce.
author: Melis
work: La Sardegna nuragica. Storia e monumenti (Corpora)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Regular complexes share construction details over wider areas than simple towers.

idea: Hierarchical territorial systems / cantons: complex nuraghi as centres drawing on several villages; at least 350 territorial systems.
author: Perra; Usai; Lo Schiavo, Perra, Usai et al.
work: Perra 2008 (via Trudu et al. 2016); Perra, Riv. Sci. Preist. 59; Sc. Antichita 15
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY for the count: Perra 2008 via Trudu et al. 2016 / Bernardini 2016
FIELD_PREDICTION: Nested site hierarchies in survey: complexes surrounded by simple towers at regular spacing.

idea: Tribal-cantonal hierarchy: canton chiefs in bastioned nuraghi, tribal chiefs above; complexes relied on contributions of several villages; inter-cantonal stone supply planned from above; obligated support from minor chiefs and villagers.
author: Ugas (summarised in Moravetti et al. 2009 and quoted by Atzeni & Frau 2023)
work: L'alba dei nuraghi; La Sardegna preistorica (compilation)
reported_only: Partly REPORTED: Ugas via Moravetti et al. 2009 and Atzeni & Frau 2023
numbers_with_locator: ~2,700 canton seats, ~50 per tribe, 8.9 km2 per canton, 4 km2 at Sardara (Moravetti et al. 2009: 361)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Storage and provisioning at canton seats; complexes built rapidly in single phases.

idea: Corvee / levy: a canton seat commands a fixed annual labour obligation from every community in its canton (not a request that can be refused).
author: Ugas (via Moravetti et al. 2009); Webster (communal labour norms)
work: Moravetti et al. 2009; Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
numbers_with_locator: 40 / 90 days per year (853); 8.9 km2 per canton (361)
implementation: Complexes (TWR >= 3, or the G3 canton seat) levy a share of the workers of every community within radius R for D days per season, acceptance = 1 (obligation), in join mode; helpers keep their own work for the rest of the season.
ranges_and_sources: R = 1.68 km (8.9 km2 canton) / 1.13 km (4 km2, Sardara) (Moravetti et al. 2009: 361); tribal R = 11.9 km (24,000 km2 / 54 tribes, PRE_NETWORKS_PLAN); D = 40 / 90 days (Webster 1991: 853); levy share 0.2 / 0.5 (ASSUMPTION)
realism_reason: Hierarchy is contested (W03); the duties are ethnographic norms, not Sardinian data.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Complexes built in one short phase (radiocarbon), while nearby simple towers show building pauses during the complex's construction.

idea: Feudal model: a large servile workforce directed by skilled master builders.
author: Lilliu
work: Sardegna nuragica (2nd ed.)
page: 44-45 (NUR review); Lilliu quoted in Sirigu et al. 2007 (note 63)
evidence_type: OPINION; Lilliu himself says size and status of the workforce are unknown (2009: 25-26)
implementation: S21_levy (central R and D, share 0.5) combined with M2 masters (vault share 0.5, pool 50): command labour plus specialists.
ranges_and_sources: as W07 and M2_central
realism_reason: No evidence of slaves or occupational specialists in excavations (Webster 1991: 840-841).
FIELD_PREDICTION: Barracks or dependent housing near complexes; workshop areas of specialist masons.

idea: Wandering crews of specialists offered their services to construction teams across the island.
author: Araque Gonzalez
work: ISLANDIA
FIELD_PREDICTION: Identical vaulting details at distant sites built at similar dates.

idea: Regional building traditions: local construction details reflect local architects and workers (regional masons, not an island pool).
author: Usai
work: Paesaggi nuragici (text republished on the Montalbano blog)
reported_only: Usai's text via a blog repost (original publication not identified)
implementation: M2 master pools confined to regions (masters walk only within their region; apprentices stay).
ranges_and_sources: regions = the 54 G133 tribes or 8 historical regions (ASSUMPTION); pool per region = M2_central (50) x site share; one new master per 20 vaults (M2 central, ASSUMPTION)
realism_reason: Regional styles are observed; master numbers are free.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Construction particulars (stair type, niches, corbel profiles) cluster in contiguous zones.

idea: No professional class of architects; no workshops of building specialists found.
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; A Prehistory of Sardinia
FIELD_PREDICTION: Continued absence of masons' workshops in excavated villages.

idea: No standard units of measurement (vs a defined unit of measure).
author: Gallin 1989 (via Webster); Scintu
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Le torri del cielo
not_testable_reason: No labour or spatial consequence in the model.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Metrological analysis of tower dimensions.

idea: Towers were built as the population grew (fission), at about 0.35% per year (Borore) or 0.42% per year (island, 1350-950 BC).
author: Webster; Ialongo
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856; Crisis and recovery (EJA 21)
implementation: Replace P10 cohorts by calendar starts: the cumulative number of started sites follows N0 exp(r t) up to 7,167; a site starts at its time whether or not earlier sites are finished. Output backlog (sites under construction) and whether communities keep up.
ranges_and_sources: r = 0.0035 / 0.0042 per year (Webster 1991: 853; Ialongo 2018: 29); span fitted so N reaches 7,167; start order random or S11 types first
realism_reason: Grounded in two demographic estimates; replaces the artificial wait-for-cohort rule.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Construction dates of nuraghi follow a smooth exponential increase, not cohorts.

idea: Island population ceilings (Ugas ~200,000 at the end of the MBA; 450,000-700,000 c. 1200 BC; Lilliu ~250,000).
author: Ugas; Lilliu (secondary)
work: L'alba dei nuraghi; secondary compilations
page: Ugas 2005: ch. 1 (page not recoverable); 450,000-700,000 via Atzeni & Frau 2023: 447 (paper draft note)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Settlement area and house counts per period (Ialongo's dwelling-area proxy) consistent with 200,000-700,000 people.

idea: Communal labour of 40 days per adult man per year (middle-range societies) or 90 days (emergent chiefdoms), in the agricultural slack season.
author: Webster (citing Erasmus 1965; Renfrew 1973)
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
scenario_label: season_days 90 in all alliance/MR runs; 40/120/210-day runs exist but are obsolete (pre-fix code; dropped by the authors 30 Oct). A 40-day rerun of MR_P10 would cost 1 run.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Seasonal markers (e.g. fauna age-at-death, crop processing) in construction layers fall in the agricultural slack period.

idea: A single tower took about 3 years at 40 days a year with the Borore labour pool; the Porcarzos additions 4-5 years (80 men x 40 days).
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
implementation: Post hoc from MR_P10 per-site outputs: per-nuraghe years for TWR1 (rescaled to 40-day seasons) and for 4-5-tower additions; compare with 3 and 4-5 years.
realism_reason: Direct comparison with the reference estimate.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Radiocarbon dates from foundation and completion deposits of single towers indistinguishable (< 10 years apart).

idea: Webster reckoned 12 years for 10 families (>= 20 adult men) for an average single tower, 25-30 years for complexes.
author: Attributed to Webster by Atzeni & Frau and an online post
work: Atzeni & Frau 2023; "Quanto tempo occorreva per costruire un nuraghe?" (post)
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY: not found in Webster 1991; reported by Atzeni & Frau 2023: 326 and an anonymous post
implementation: As R01: compare MR_P10 per-nuraghe years with 12 and 25-30 years.
realism_reason: Misattributed or garbled figure; useful only as a popular benchmark.
FIELD_PREDICTION: As R01.

idea: Nuraghe construction took a modest share of labour: about 2.5% of adult male time (9.5 days a year), even if doubled.
author: Webster
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
implementation: Post hoc: MR_P10 island man-hours per year / (adult male population x working hours), using the population ceiling and Webster's 1 adult male per 5 people.
ranges_and_sources: 1 adult male per 5 (Webster 1991: 853)
realism_reason: Same quantity as Webster's.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Not directly observable; indirectly, construction spans of neighbouring single towers should rarely overlap if each man gave ~2.5% of his time.

idea: 8,000 nuraghi + 700 giants' tombs over 600 years = 11.5 simple and 1.86 complex nuraghi a year, ~4,160 people at ~208 sites, 1.66% of 250,000 able-bodied.
author: Atzeni & Frau
work: book (compilation, non-specialist)
implementation: Post hoc: MR_P10 mean concurrent building sites and workforce per year vs 208 sites / 4,160 people.
realism_reason: Back-of-envelope figures by non-specialists.
FIELD_PREDICTION: At any time ~200 towers under construction island-wide: radiocarbon construction dates should show that many overlapping building events per generation.

idea: A systematic programme of building nuraghi and villages persisted for 700 years (c. 1600-900 BC).
author: Ugas (summarised in Moravetti et al.)
work: La Sardegna preistorica (compilation)
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY: Ugas via Moravetti et al. 2009
implementation: Post hoc: compare MR_P10/P20 island years with 700 years as well as Ialongo's ~500 (Ialongo 2018).
realism_reason: A second chronological target.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Dated foundations spread over 1600-900 BC.

idea: Experimental 20-year build of a trilobate nuraghe with period technology (NurTime, Gergei).
author: NurTime project (Perdas Novas; Ollanu; Auguadro)
work: L'Unione Sarda 9 Oct 2023; NURTIME (nurnet.net)
implementation: Single-site runs (not MR_P10) for a 3-tower nuraghe at Gergei with the NurTime crew size and calendar, under MR technique and the lift variants (S4a/b/c/d/e), to publish predictions of crew, man-hours and years before the experiment reports.
ranges_and_sources: crew and days per year: to be taken from NurTime when available (unknown now)
realism_reason: A pre-registered prediction is the cleanest validation route.
FIELD_PREDICTION: The NurTime build should record person-hours per stage, crew per block and placing rates that fall inside the model's predicted ranges.

idea: Unfinished nuraghi exist (only the first ring course and the entrance lintel laid), abandoned when the social structure that started them failed.
author: Atzeni, A.
work: La monetazione nella Sardegna nuragica (Condaghes)
evidence_type: EVIDENCE: field observation (Mura Era I, Sindia; Portazo, Sedilo) + interpretation
implementation: Post hoc: from MR_P10 per-site outputs, flag sites whose build span exceeds one generation (25 years) or whose party cannot move the lintel (S20); map them and compare with known unfinished nuraghi.
ranges_and_sources: 25 years (ASSUMPTION, one generation)
realism_reason: Real field category; the generation threshold is assumed.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Unfinished nuraghi concentrate among sites the model predicts slow (small parties, long hauls); the lintel is placed with the first course.

idea: Nuraghe stone reused in Punic, Roman and later buildings; nuraghi dismantled.
author: Floris; Delussu (in Trudu et al.); Usai, D.
work: Il tofet di Tharros; Le torri nuragiche oltre l'eta del Bronzo; Il gigante del Parteolla
not_testable_reason: Post-Nuragic: no consequence for how the nuraghi were built (affects only today's heights and tower counts).
FIELD_PREDICTION: Dressed nuragic blocks built into later Punic, Roman and medieval structures near nuraghi (no prediction about construction).

idea: Upper stones and clay bricks were removed for new buildings in the Middle Ages (S'Urachi).
author: Chiri & Novelli
work: as M04
not_testable_reason: Post-Nuragic; an input-data issue (original heights), not a building mechanism.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Medieval buildings near S'Urachi contain its basalt blocks and brick (no prediction about construction).

idea: Stone of abandoned nuraghi reused for later Nuragic building (villages, other towers).
author: (implied by Ialongo's abandonment figures)
work: Ialongo 2018, EJA 21
not_testable_reason: Data missing: no evidence that Nuragic builders robbed abandoned towers; abandonment mostly postdates the building phase.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Tower blocks with earlier mortar or dressing reused in later huts.

idea: Ancient collapses and restorations: Ponte (dressed limestone in the upper parts), Su Nuraxi re-facing after ground slippage, Nuraxi 'e Cresia keep and bastion collapsed and the plan completed in basalt only.
author: Foddai; Lilliu; Murru
work: Il nuraghe Santu Antine della piana del Riu Mannu; I nuraghi; Nuraxi 'e Cresia (in Perra & Cicilloni eds)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Rebuilt sectors in a different stone or technique on top of collapse debris.

idea: Many nuraghi collapsed and more than 6 in 10 were abandoned at the end of the Bronze Age.
author: Nieddu, Atzeni et al.
work: Il nuraghe San Marco-Genuri: il riuso tra Bronzo finale ...
FIELD_PREDICTION: Collapse layers dated to the Final Bronze-Early Iron Age at most abandoned towers.

idea: Upper parts collapsed through neglect after abandonment (vegetation, thermal cycling, rain).
author: Atzeni & Frau
work: book
not_testable_reason: Post-use process; no consequence for construction labour.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Collapse deposits post-date abandonment, with soil and root channels between fallen blocks.

idea: Food and drink consumed in feasts by the associated communities; catering by farmers and shepherds was a building role; chiefs' generosity and banquets.
author: Araque Gonzalez; Webster
work: ISLANDIA; Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia [IT-wt]
scenario_label: S12_low / s10 / central / s30 / high (food cap: the host feeds its hands)
realism_1_5: 2 (existing ratings; S12 runs give 2,231-7,503 island years)
FIELD_PREDICTION: Feasting deposits (large-animal bones, serving vessels) in construction-phase layers.

idea: Work feasts attract helpers: hosts with more food draw more outside labour (feast as incentive, not as cap).
author: Dietrich et al. (after Dietler & Herbich 2001); applied to nuraghi by Araque Gonzalez
work: Cereal processing at Early Neolithic Gobekli Tepe; ISLANDIA
page: Dietrich et al. 2019: page not recoverable; Araque Gonzalez 2021: 193-194
implementation: Add beta4 x host surplus (S12 food-capacity catchments, central values) to the acceptance logistic; no hard food cap.
ranges_and_sources: beta4 = 0.5 / 2 per tonne of annual surplus (ASSUMPTION); surplus from S12 central (tools/food_capacity.py)
realism_reason: Widely documented mechanism, no Sardinian quantity.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Complexes with large feasting and storage deposits (ziri) dated to their construction phase; consumers of varied origin (isotopes).

idea: Federal sanctuaries were nodes of the local economic system; sanctuaries replaced nuraghi as social catalysts.
author: Moravetti et al. (eds); Nurnet "Bella eta" article
work: La Sardegna nuragica. Storia e materiali; nurnet.net
page: Moravetti et al. 2014: 461-462; web, no page
not_testable_reason: Chronology: federal sanctuaries date from c. 950 BC, after most nuraghe building (Ialongo 2018); no consequence for tower construction.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Sanctuary construction dates later than nuraghe construction in the same territory.

idea: Political centralisation: complex nuraghi as hubs that coordinate the smaller towers.
author: Ugas (via Moravetti et al.); Lo Schiavo et al.
work: Moravetti et al. 2009; Sc. Antichita 15
reported_only: REPORTED-ONLY: Ugas via Moravetti et al. 2009
FIELD_PREDICTION: Help and provisioning concentrated at hubs (model: hubs give 62-91% of help).

idea: Polycentric communities: nuraghi in clouds or chains, cooperating on several levels; competitive emulation between neighbours.
author: Usai; Trump (via Webster)
work: Paesaggi nuragici (blog repost); Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia
page: Usai: blog, no page; Webster 2015: page not verified
reported_only: Trump's emulation idea REPORTED via Webster 2015 (page not verified)
scenario_label: M1_s1_R5 and M1 variants (emulation); P_G20 / G133 groups
FIELD_PREDICTION: Build dates cluster in space and time (neighbour cohorts).

idea: Stone was local: only 7 of 113 Marghine nuraghi used stone from more than 2 km away.
author: Gallin 1989 (via Webster)
work: Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
implementation: Post hoc: share of Marghine sites (Gallin's area) with hybrid-rule haul > 2 km in the MR_P10 summary; target 6%.
realism_reason: An independent field statistic the model has not yet been checked against.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Model share of Marghine sites with > 2 km hauls close to 6%.

idea: Sites were chosen for near-surface building stone (and water), on least-cost principles.
author: Webster
work: Duos Nuraghes vol. 1; Archaeology of Nuragic Sardinia
scenario_label: hybrid stone rule (4,940 sites on own outcrop; 99.95% agreement with recorded stone)
FIELD_PREDICTION: As Q01.

idea: Strategic position mattered more than suitable rock; most Nurri-Orroli fortresses used local rock, but site importance could override the need to fetch stone elsewhere.
author: Orgiana
work: Tecniche, forme costruttive ed evoluzione nei nuraghi del Sarcidano (ArcheoArte suppl.)
numbers_with_locator: > 67% of 79 related to giare; 26.5% on reliefs
implementation: Post hoc: model haul and stone class for the Nurri and Orroli sites vs Orgiana's finding (local rock except one tower).
realism_reason: Local check with a published survey.
FIELD_PREDICTION: The one non-local tower in Orgiana's sample should be a long-haul site in the model.

idea: Builders used whatever local rock existed (basalt, trachyte, granite, limestone, marl); towers rarely stand on stone-poor colluvium.
author: Tran et al.; Lilliu & Zucca; Foddai
work: Physical digital twins ... nuraghi (C. R. Mecanique 353); Su Nuraxi di Barumini; Il nuraghe Santu Antine della piana del Riu Mannu
page: Tran et al. 2025: 802-803; Lilliu & Zucca 2005: ~10-11; Foddai 2014: page not recoverable (near n. 72)
FIELD_PREDICTION: As Q01.

idea: Mixed and bichrome masonry: light limestone inserts or upper courses on basalt towers (Santu Antine, S'Urachi antemural, Su Nuraxi tower C), mixed limestone-basalt towers.
author: Foddai; Stiglitz, Dies Cusi et al.; Paglietti & Mulas
work: Santu Antine della piana del Riu Mannu; Quaderni 26/2015; Layers 8
page: Foddai 2014: page not recoverable; Stiglitz et al. 2015: page not recoverable; Paglietti & Mulas 2023: 234
implementation: On complexes with fine facing, a share b of the upper facing blocks comes from the nearest outcrop of a contrasting stone class (one extra multi-source Dijkstra per class set, as the hybrid rule).
ranges_and_sources: b = 0.05 / 0.15 of facing blocks (ASSUMPTION); class pairs basalt->limestone/marl, limestone->basalt (ASSUMPTION)
realism_reason: Bichromy is attested; share and frequency unknown.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Provenance of light inserts to the nearest contrasting outcrop; their haul distance longer than the wall stone's.

idea: Site-level provenance: Su Nuraxi phase-a basalt "recovered" from the slope towards nuraghe Marfudi; S'Urachi basalt ~3 km; Duos from its own knoll.
author: Lilliu & Zucca; Stiglitz et al.; Webster
work: Su Nuraxi di Barumini; Atti XLIV RS IIPP; Webster 1991, Antiquity 65: 840-856
page: Lilliu & Zucca 2005: 40-41; Stiglitz et al. 2012: 921-922; Webster 1991: 848
implementation: Post hoc: model quarry location and haul for Su Nuraxi, S'Urachi and Duos vs the published sources.
realism_reason: Site-level validation with the best evidence.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Model quarry cells within a few hundred metres (Su Nuraxi, Duos) and ~3 km (S'Urachi).

idea: Tower size varies: chamber diameter 2.5-7 m (mode 4.2-4.6 m); of 130 nuraghi, 58% keep 1 residual floor, 38% 2, 4% 3; a first-floor chamber needs a cone diameter > 8.3 m.
author: Atzeni & Frau
work: book (compilation)
evidence_type: Survey statistics (source of the sample not given)
implementation: Draw each single tower's tonnage from a floor-count distribution (1 floor 0.6x, 2 floors 1.0x, 3 floors 1.4x of 1,350 t; ASSUMPTION) instead of a fixed 1,350 t.
ranges_and_sources: shares 58/38/4% (Atzeni & Frau 2023: 326; residual, not original floors); tonnage factors ASSUMPTION
realism_reason: Residual floors understate original height; the sample source is not stated.
FIELD_PREDICTION: Collapse volumes around towers indicate original heights.
